- **Essay clusters:** linked Notes that form a 2–4 note thread on a single idea
- **Threads worth carrying forward**
- **Unlabeled-speaker meetings:** while reading `Inbox/meetings/*.md`, grep for `Speaker 1`, `Speaker 2`, `Speaker 3` (etc.) patterns. Track which meeting files still have unnamed speakers. The user labels speakers manually in the Fireflies web UI — no API for it — so the review's job is just to flag them.

**Curation rule:** if you can't name a theme/project/decision in one sentence with a source citation, drop it. The review is for the user's working memory, not for completeness.

## Step 4 — Write the review note

File: `Inbox/weekly-review/YYYY-MM-DD-review.md` (use today's date — Friday or whenever invoked).

Start from `Templates/weekly-review.md` and fill it in. Sections:

0. **Last week's three priorities — did they happen?** — one line per priority from the previous review: yes / partly / no, with the evidence. **No-movement warning:** a priority has *movement* when this week shows a commit that changes the work itself (STATUS-only and closeout-sweep commits do not count), a new line in `output/_ledger.md`, or a new date written down. A priority with none of the three gets a banner as the first line under the note's title: `> ⚠ NO MOVEMENT — week N: <priority>`. N counts the consecutive reviews it appeared in without movement (read back through earlier reviews). At week 3, its line in **Next week — priorities** must be ship by a named date, re-date in writing, or park; carrying it as-is is the drift.
1. **Themes recurring this week** — bulleted, each with source citation `[[file]]` or `(meeting: X, date)`.
2. **Active projects — status snapshot** — markdown table with columns: Project | Status (progressing / drifting / stuck / decided / new) | Last touched | Note. Be ruthless about marking "drifting" — that's the value of this whole exercise.
3. **Decisions made this week** — bulleted, quote the decision in the user's words if available, with source citation.
4. **Open action items (stale > 14d flagged)** — from `action-items list`. Each line: owner — task — age — source meeting. Flag stale items with `⚠`.
5. **Essay angles emerging** — each angle: working title, 1-sentence thesis, list of 2–4 `[[Note]]` links that support it. These are candidates for moving into `Drafts/`.
6. **Next week — priorities and why** — three items, ranked. One sentence per item on why this beats the alternatives. **This is the most important section.** Push back on the user if their answer here is generic ("keep working on X").
7. **Open threads to revisit** — anything noticed but not actioned.
8. **Pipeline hygiene** (only include if there's something to flag):
   - Unlabeled speakers in this week's meetings — list the affected meeting files with a single-line action: *"Open in Fireflies UI and assign names to Speaker N entries."*
   - Generic-titled meetings still in the local DB — suggest running `/name-meetings` if any appeared this week.
   - Registry drift — the Step 1 one-liner, if the count is above zero.
   - Friday sweep — the Step 4b line.
   - Skip this section entirely if all of these are clean.

Update frontmatter counts: `meetings_reviewed`, `interviews_reviewed`, `notes_touched`.

## Step 4b — Friday sweep (paused projects that went quiet)

PM system design Decision 6: paused projects untouched for 30+ days get a decision, 10 a week, oldest first, so the paused backlog clears instead of growing. Run:

```
python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py sweep
```

It prints up to 10 rows with lane, receiver and last-known date, plus how many are pending in all (the live board's header shows the same count). Put the list to Eric in one message and take his answer for each, in one reply:

- **revive**: back on the board. Needs a concrete next step, and for job/side/tool a receiver (a name, or `me: <why>`). The slate cap and the 7-day clock apply.
- **keep**: stays paused; out of the sweep for 90 days.
- **archive**: retired.

Apply each with `portfolio.py sweep-decide <name> revive|keep|archive [--next-action "<step>"] [--receiver "<who>"]`. A revive refused for the cap or a missing receiver: tell Eric and ask again, never fill a receiver in for him. Anything he doesn't decide comes back next week on its own; do not chase it. Commit the registry in project-triage as `data: sweep <YYYY-MM-DD>` and push. Add one line to the note's **Pipeline hygiene**: `Sweep: N revived, N kept, N archived, N still pending`.

## Step 4c — Session sweep (clear the home screen)

Sessions are scratchpads; the repo and each `docs/STATUS.md` are the record. Run the read-only sweep:

```
python ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py
```

It prints KEEP (running, finished <24 h ago, or holding a worktree), SAFE TO DELETE, and repos with unsaved work. Show Eric the SAFE list in one message and ask once. On yes, run `claude rm <id>` for each SAFE id (it refuses a session whose worktree has unpushed work; report any refusal, never force it). Never delete a KEEP session or `rm` a `~/.claude/jobs/` folder by hand. Repos with unsaved work go to `/closeout`, not into kept sessions. Add one line to **Pipeline hygiene**: `Sessions: N deleted, N kept`.

## Step 4d — Inbox drain (`~/DEV/_INBOX` and `~/Downloads`)

An inbox with no drain is a second archive. List what has sat for a week:

```
find ~/DEV/_INBOX ~/Downloads -maxdepth 1 -mtime +7 -not -name '.*' -not -name tools -not -name docs -not -name drain-reports
```

Each entry has exactly one home: its project repo, `~/DEV/_DRIVE/` by the ladder in `_DRIVE/README.md` (folder = stage, filename = subject), or `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`. Move it there (one file through the Drive mount is fine; big trees go by the Drive MCP). A `from-<copy>/` folder counts as one entry; its README names the homes. Done when both folders hold nothing older than 7 days. Report the two counts.

## Step 4e — Monthly feedback look-back (first review of the month)

When today's day of the month is 7 or less, run the feedback look-back in `FEEDBACK.md` (beside this file) and add its section to the review note. Other weeks, skip this step.

## Step 5 — Sign off

Brief summary to user (3–5 lines):
- File written: path
- Headline number: N meetings, M interviews, K notes synthesized
- The three priorities you proposed for next week
- One open question worth them thinking about before next Monday

## Step 6 — Offer (don't take) the next move

After delivering the review, offer:
> "Want me to start a `Drafts/<essay-slug>.md` from one of the essay angles? Or carry any of the stale action items into a tomorrow-morning agenda?"

Do not auto-create drafts. The user picks.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't generate a review without meeting-sync running first.** Stale data = wrong priorities.
- **Don't pad sections to fill the template.** A short, honest review beats a long, padded one. If "decisions made" is empty, write "None this week." and move on.
- **Don't include items you can't cite.** Every claim → source.
- **Don't write to `Drafts/` automatically.** Drafts are a deliberate user choice.
- **Don't run weekly-review more than once per week** unless the user explicitly asks (e.g., "redo the review with X added"). Repeated runs erode the ritual.

# Skill mechanics

The skill-specific branch of [`writing-for-agents`](SKILL.md): what changes when the document is a skill (frontmatter, the invocation choice, and router skills). Everything else about writing it is the universal reference in `SKILL.md`.

## Invocation

Two choices, trading the two loads:

- A **model-invoked** skill keeps a `description`, so the agent can fire it autonomously, and other skills can reach it. You can still type its name: model-invocation always _includes_ user reach; a description only ever adds agent discovery, never removes the human's. The description is the skill's top-level context pointer, forced to stay loaded at all times: permanent context load in exchange for discoverability. A model-invoked skill whose content is all reference is also one home for shared reference: another skill can invoke it, so reference needed by several skills lives in one place. Mechanics: omit `disable-model-invocation`, and write a model-facing description carrying the trigger branches (the pointer-writing rules in `SKILL.md` apply in full).
- A **user-invoked** skill strips the description from the agent's reach: only the human typing its name can invoke it, and no other skill can. Zero context load, but it spends cognitive load: you are the index that must remember it exists. Mechanics: set `disable-model-invocation: true`; the `description` becomes human-facing: a one-line summary, trigger lists stripped.

Pick model-invocation only when the agent must reach the skill on its own, or another skill must. If it only ever fires by hand, make it user-invoked and pay no context load.

Shared reference that two user-invoked skills both need can live in neither: with no descriptions, neither can fire the other. Push it to a plain file outside the skill system: external reference any skill can point at.

## Splitting by invocation

The invocation cut of splitting (the sequence cut lives in `SKILL.md`): split off a model-invoked skill when you have a distinct leading word that should trigger it on its own (a trigger word you actually use in your prompts), or another skill must reach it. You pay context load for the new always-loaded description, so that independent reach has to be worth it.

## Router skills

When user-invoked skills multiply past what you can remember, that piled-up cognitive load is cured by a **router skill**: one user-invoked skill that names the others and when to reach for each, so the human has one skill to remember instead of many. It can only hint, never fire them: user-invoked skills have no description, so nothing but the human can reach them.

# Monthly feedback look-back

Pulls the feedback other people gave Eric in the last 30 days, groups it by theme, and names the top 3 ways he can improve. Runs inside the first weekly review of each month. Added 2026-10-22 from Austin Marchese's "4 things" video (strategy 3, feedback loops); the first run was done by hand the same day.

## Privacy first

Meeting dialogue is other people's words. Eric approves the read at the start of each run ("approved, read the meetings"); the auto-mode classifier blocks it without that. Then:

- Process transcripts inside a context-mode sandbox (`ctx_execute`). Print only the turns you need. Write no transcript, summary or excerpt to disk.
- Quote only what is said to or about Eric. Leave athlete names and health details out of the note.

## Sources

| Source | How | Reach |
|---|---|---|
| Fireflies | Pick meetings from the local DB `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db` (`transcripts` table, `date_string >= <30 days ago>`, `json_extract(data,'$.summary.overview')`, `speakers`). Get dialogue with `fireflies-pp-cli transcripts get <id> --live --json` and merge `sentences` into turns by `speaker_name`. | Main source |
| Gmail | `search_threads` with `after:<date> -category:promotions -category:social -category:updates -category:forums (feedback OR thanks OR appreciate OR suggestion OR concern)` | Personal account only; usually empty |
| Outlook, Teams | Not reachable from the Mac. Say so in the note. | None |

Skip church meetings (`CABC`, `Sermon`) and vendor demos or talks Eric only attended.

## Method

1. **1-on-1s** (Kenny, Carrie, Jason and similar): read every turn of the other person over 60 characters. This is where most feedback lives.
2. **Group meetings** (staff, SA Leadership): read only the turns by others that name Eric.
3. Sort each piece into **praise**, **asks** (what someone wants from Eric) or **corrections**. Separate complaints about third parties from feedback to Eric.
4. Group into 2–4 themes. Each item needs who, date and a short quote.

Done when every 1-on-1 in the window has been read and every theme has at least one quote.

## Output

Add a section **Feedback look-back (monthly)** to the review note, after **Decisions made this week**:

- **Praise**: quotes with who and date.
- **Themes**: each with 1–3 quotes.
- **Top 3 to improve**: one concrete habit each.
- **Since last month**: did last month's top 3 come up again? Find them in the newest `Inbox/weekly-review/` note holding a "Feedback look-back" section (the first run is `2026-10-22-feedback-lookback.md`).
- **Coverage**: meetings read, sources not reached.

Put the top 3 in the Step 5 sign-off.

Shows a digest of all meetings in the lookback window:
titles, gist summaries, topics, and action items aggregated in one view.
Designed as the entry point for a morning sync or cron job.

Usage:
  fireflies-pp-cli digest [flags]

Examples:
  fireflies-pp-cli digest
  fireflies-pp-cli digest --since 48h
  fireflies-pp-cli digest --since 24h --processed-only --json

Flags:
      --db string        Database path

---
name: weekly-review
description: >-
  Friday close-of-week ritual: syncs meetings, runs the weekly housekeeping sweeps, and
  writes one review note in the SecondBrain vault that names next week's three
  priorities. Use when user says "/weekly-review", "weekly review", "Friday review",
  "let's do this week's review", "weekly synthesis", or "what should I work on next
  week?". Do not use for the end-of-day interview (use interview-me) or the biweekly
  supervisor report (use status-report).
---

# Weekly Review

End-of-week synthesis and Eric's **project prioritization surface**: it names what is progressing, what is drifting, and the three things that earn next week. One run per week; rerun only when Eric asks (e.g. "redo the review with X added").

Paths come from `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`: `vault_root`, `vault_output_ledger`, `portfolio_json`. Vault paths below are relative to `vault_root`. `$PT` below means the folder holding `portfolio_json`.

## Step 1 — Refresh meetings

Invoke the `meeting-sync` skill. If it reports auth failure, stop and give Eric its auth message: the review needs current meeting data.

## Step 2 — Gather (read-only)

Run all of these before asking Eric anything. Keep each result for the note.

1. **Filename drift** (its weekly home; too slow for every sync):
   `python3 ~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/audit_filenames.py --since $(date -v-90d +%F)`
   Keep only `regression_count` and `semantic_count`. Renames are fixed upstream in Fireflies or by Eric; meeting-sync's Drift audit section says what each class means.
2. **Registry drift**: `python3 $PT/portfolio.py crosswalk --json`. Count `problems` by `kind`. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive half did not run: say that, not zero. A DEV folder with no row is a project started outside the list; name it in **Next week — priorities** if it is real work.
3. **Paused sweep** (PM system design Decision 6: paused projects untouched 30+ days get a decision, 10 a week, oldest first): `python3 $PT/portfolio.py sweep`. It prints up to 10 rows with lane, receiver and last-known date, plus the total pending.
4. **Sessions**: `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py`. It prints KEEP, SAFE TO DELETE, and repos with unsaved work.
5. **Inbox** (an inbox with no drain is a second archive):
   `find ~/DEV/_INBOX ~/Downloads -maxdepth 1 -mtime +7 -not -name '.*' -not -name tools -not -name docs -not -name drain-reports`
   Give each entry its one home: its project repo, `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`, or Drive (`~/DEV/_DRIVE` is the Drive mount; its `README.md` has the ladder: folder = stage, filename = subject). A `from-<copy>/` folder is one entry; its README names the homes.
6. **Vault inputs**, by mtime, last 7 days: `Inbox/meetings/*.md`, `Inbox/*-interview.md`, `Notes/*.md`.
7. **Fireflies**. `--agent` implies `--compact`, which strips `action-items` and `topics` rows to `{}`, so those two run with `--json` alone:
   ```bash
   fireflies-pp-cli digest --since 7d --processed-only --json --agent
   fireflies-pp-cli action-items list --from 30 --json
   fireflies-pp-cli topics list --from 7 --json
   ```
8. **Unnamed speakers**. Vault notes hold summaries only, so read the live transcript. For each digest `id`, this prints the title and `UNNAMED` or `ok`, and keeps the dialogue out of context:
   ```bash
   fireflies-pp-cli transcripts get <id> --live --json | python3 -c "import json,re,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d=d.get('data',d); print(d.get('title'), '->', 'UNNAMED' if any(re.fullmatch(r'Speaker \d+', s.get('speaker_name') or '') for s in d.get('sentences') or []) else 'ok')"
   ```

## Step 3 — One ask, a pick on every line

Put every question in one message, each with your recommended answer, so Eric can reply "all as recommended" or change one line:

- **Each sweep row**: revive, keep (out of the sweep for 90 days) or archive. Recommend keep unless the row shows work this month. A revive needs a concrete next step and, for job/side/tool, a receiver (a name, or `me: <why>`); the slate cap and the 7-day clock apply.
- **Sessions**: delete the SAFE list? Recommend yes.
- **Feedback look-back**, first review of the month only (day of month 7 or less): approve reading the meetings? Recommend yes. `FEEDBACK.md` (beside this file) holds the method and privacy rules.

## Step 4 — Apply the answers

- **Sweep**: `python3 $PT/portfolio.py sweep-decide <name> revive|keep|archive [--next-action "<step>"] [--receiver "<who>"]`. A revive refused for the cap or a missing receiver goes back to Eric; the receiver is always his words. Rows he leaves undecided return next week on their own. Commit the registry in project-triage as `data: sweep <YYYY-MM-DD>` and push.
- **Sessions**: `claude rm <id>` for each SAFE id. It refuses a session whose worktree has unpushed work: report the refusal and leave the session. Sessions leave only by `claude rm` of a SAFE id; KEEP sessions and `~/.claude/jobs/` folders stay. Repos with unsaved work go to `/closeout`.
- **Inbox**: move up to 10 entries whose home is a repo or `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`. Drive-bound entries are counted, not moved: the Drive mount hangs on reads, so they go by the Drive MCP or `gws` in their own session.
- **Feedback look-back**, if approved: run `FEEDBACK.md`.

## Step 5 — Synthesize

Read each Step 2 input and build:

- **Theme map**: topics in 2+ sources.
- **Project map**: each named project progressed (decision made, work shipped), drifted (mentioned, no movement), or stuck (blocked, awaiting input).
- **Decision log**: decision sentences across all sources.
- **Stale action items**: Fireflies has no done flag. An item from a meeting 14–30 days old is stale (⚠) unless a source from this week (a `docs/STATUS.md`, the output ledger, a newer meeting) shows it done.
- **Essay clusters**: 2–4 linked Notes on one idea.
- **Movement** on last week's three priorities: a commit that changes the work itself (STATUS-only and closeout-sweep commits do not count), a new line in the output ledger, or a new date written down.

**Curation rule:** a theme, project or decision you cannot state in one sentence with a source citation is dropped. The review is Eric's working memory, not a complete record.

## Step 6 — Write the note

Write `Inbox/weekly-review/YYYY-MM-DD-review.md` (today's date) once, from `Templates/weekly-review.md`, with every Step 2–5 result in it. A section with nothing in it reads "None this week." Every claim carries a source: `[[file]]` or `(meeting: X, date)`.

0. **Last week's three priorities — did they happen?** One line per priority from the previous review: yes / partly / no, with the evidence. A priority with no movement gets a banner as the first line under the note's title: `> ⚠ NO MOVEMENT — week N: <priority>`. N counts the consecutive reviews it appeared in without movement (read back through earlier reviews). At week 3, its line in **Next week — priorities** must be ship by a named date, re-date in writing, or park; carrying it as-is is the drift.
1. **Themes recurring this week**, each with its source.
2. **Active projects — status snapshot**: table of Project | Status (progressing / drifting / stuck / decided / new) | Last touched | Note. Mark "drifting" ruthlessly: that is the value of the exercise.
3. **Decisions made this week**, in Eric's words where available. When the look-back ran, the **Feedback look-back (monthly)** section follows this one (format in `FEEDBACK.md`).
4. **Open action items (stale > 14d flagged)**: owner — task — age — source meeting, ⚠ on stale.
5. **Essay angles emerging**: working title, one-sentence thesis, 2–4 `[[Note]]` links. Candidates for `Drafts/`.
6. **Next week — priorities and why**: three items, ranked, one sentence each on why it beats the alternatives. **The most important section.** Push back if Eric's answer is generic ("keep working on X").
7. **Open threads to revisit**: noticed, not actioned.
8. **Pipeline hygiene**: one line for each item that is not clean; omit the section when all are clean.
   - Meeting filenames: N regressions, N semantic diffs — see meeting-sync drift audit.
   - Registry drift: counts by kind — run `portfolio.py crosswalk`.
   - Unnamed speakers: the UNNAMED meeting titles — "Open in Fireflies and name the Speaker N entries" (Fireflies has no API for it).
   - Generic-titled meetings still in the local DB: suggest `/name-meetings`.
   - Sweep: N revived, N kept, N archived, N still pending (registry commit sha).
   - Sessions: N deleted, N kept.
   - Inbox: N moved; N left in `_INBOX`, N in `~/Downloads`, N of them Drive-bound; up or down from last week.

Set the frontmatter counts: `meetings_reviewed`, `interviews_reviewed`, `notes_touched`.

**Done when** the note exists with every section filled or "None this week.", every non-clean Step 2 result has its Pipeline hygiene line, the frontmatter counts are set, Eric's sweep answers are applied and pushed, and **Next week** holds three ranked priorities, each with its why.

## Step 7 — Sign off

Three to five lines:

- File written: path.
- N meetings, M interviews, K notes synthesized.
- The three priorities for next week.
- The one open decision, with your recommended answer.
- The look-back's top 3, when it ran.

Then offer, and wait: start a `Drafts/<essay-slug>.md` from one essay angle, or carry stale action items into tomorrow's agenda. A draft is written only when Eric picks one.

# Monthly feedback look-back

Pulls the feedback other people gave Eric in the last 30 days, groups it by theme, and names the top 3 ways he can improve. Runs inside the first weekly review of each month. Added 2026-10-22 from Austin Marchese's "4 things" video (strategy 3, feedback loops); the first run was done by hand the same day.

## Privacy first

Meeting dialogue is other people's words. Eric approves the read at the start of each run ("approved, read the meetings"); the auto-mode classifier blocks it without that. Then:

- Process transcripts inside a context-mode sandbox (`ctx_execute`). Print only the turns you need. Write no transcript, summary or excerpt to disk.
- Quote only what is said to or about Eric. Leave athlete names and health details out of the note.

## Sources

| Source | How | Reach |
|---|---|---|
| Fireflies | Pick meetings from the local DB `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db` (`transcripts` table, `date_string >= <30 days ago>`, `json_extract(data,'$.summary.overview')`, `speakers`). Get dialogue with `fireflies-pp-cli transcripts get <id> --live --json` and merge `sentences` into turns by `speaker_name`. | Main source |
| Gmail | `search_threads` with `after:<date> -category:promotions -category:social -category:updates -category:forums (feedback OR thanks OR appreciate OR suggestion OR concern)` | Personal account only; usually empty |
| Outlook, Teams | Not reachable from the Mac. Say so in the note. | None |

Skip church meetings (`CABC`, `Sermon`) and vendor demos or talks Eric only attended.

## Method

1. **1-on-1s** (Kenny, Carrie, Jason and similar): read every turn of the other person over 60 characters. This is where most feedback lives.
2. **Group meetings** (staff, SA Leadership): read only the turns by others that name Eric.
3. Sort each piece into **praise**, **asks** (what someone wants from Eric) or **corrections**. Separate complaints about third parties from feedback to Eric.
4. Group into 2–4 themes. Each item needs who, date and a short quote.

Done when every 1-on-1 in the window has been read and every theme has at least one quote.

## Output

Add a section **Feedback look-back (monthly)** to the review note, after **Decisions made this week**:

- **Praise**: quotes with who and date.
- **Themes**: each with 1–3 quotes.
- **Top 3 to improve**: one concrete habit each.
- **Since last month**: did last month's top 3 come up again? Find them in the newest `Inbox/weekly-review/` note holding a "Feedback look-back" section (the first run is `2026-10-22-feedback-lookback.md`).
- **Coverage**: meetings read, sources not reached.

Put the top 3 in the Step 5 sign-off.

name: weekly-review
description: >-
  Friday close-of-week ritual: syncs meetings, runs the weekly housekeeping sweeps, and
  writes one review note in the SecondBrain vault that names next week's three
  priorities. Use when user says "/weekly-review", "weekly review", "Friday review",
  "let's do this week's review", "weekly synthesis", or "what should I work on next
  week?". Do not use for the end-of-day interview (use interview-me) or the biweekly
  supervisor report (use status-report).
---

# Weekly Review

End-of-week synthesis and Eric's **project prioritization surface**: it names what is progressing, what is drifting, and the three things that earn next week. One run per week; rerun only when Eric asks (e.g. "redo the review with X added").

Paths come from `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`: `vault_root`, `vault_output_ledger`, `portfolio_json`. Vault paths below are relative to `vault_root`. `$PT` below means the folder holding `portfolio_json`.

## Step 1 — Refresh meetings

Invoke the `meeting-sync` skill. If it reports auth failure, stop and give Eric its auth message: the review needs current meeting data.

## Step 2 — Gather (read-only)

Run all of these before asking Eric anything. Keep each result for the note.

1. **Filename drift** (its weekly home; too slow for every sync):
   `python3 ~/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/audit_filenames.py --since $(date -v-90d +%F)`
   Keep only `regression_count` and `semantic_count`. Renames are fixed upstream in Fireflies or by Eric; meeting-sync's Drift audit section says what each class means.
2. **Registry drift**: `python3 $PT/portfolio.py crosswalk --json`. Count `problems` by `kind`. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive half did not run: say that, not zero. A DEV folder with no row is a project started outside the list; name it in **Next week — priorities** if it is real work.
3. **Paused sweep** (PM system design Decision 6: paused projects untouched 30+ days get a decision, 10 a week, oldest first): `python3 $PT/portfolio.py sweep`. It prints up to 10 rows with lane, receiver and last-known date, plus the total pending.
4. **Sessions**: `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py`. It prints KEEP, SAFE TO DELETE, and repos with unsaved work.
5. **Inbox** (an inbox with no drain is a second archive):
   `find ~/DEV/_INBOX ~/Downloads -maxdepth 1 -mtime +7 -not -name '.*' -not -name tools -not -name docs -not -name drain-reports`
   Give each entry its one home: its project repo, `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`, or Drive (`~/DEV/_DRIVE` is the Drive mount; its `README.md` has the ladder: folder = stage, filename = subject). A `from-<copy>/` folder is one entry; its README names the homes.
6. **Vault inputs**, by mtime, last 7 days: `Inbox/meetings/*.md`, `Inbox/*-interview.md`, `Notes/*.md`.
7. **Fireflies**. `--agent` implies `--compact`, which strips `action-items` and `topics` rows to `{}`, so those two run with `--json` alone:
   ```bash
   fireflies-pp-cli digest --since 7d --processed-only --json --agent
   fireflies-pp-cli action-items list --from 30 --json
   fireflies-pp-cli topics list --from 7 --json
   ```
8. **Unnamed speakers**. Vault notes hold summaries only, so read the live transcript. For each digest `id`, this prints the title and `UNNAMED` or `ok`, and keeps the dialogue out of context:
   ```bash
   fireflies-pp-cli transcripts get <id> --live --json | python3 -c "import json,re,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); d=d.get('data',d); print(d.get('title'), '->', 'UNNAMED' if any(re.fullmatch(r'Speaker \d+', s.get('speaker_name') or '') for s in d.get('sentences') or []) else 'ok')"
   ```

## Step 3 — One ask, a pick on every line

Put every question in one message, each with your recommended answer, so Eric can reply "all as recommended" or change one line:

- **Each sweep row**: revive, keep (out of the sweep for 90 days) or archive. Recommend keep unless the row shows work this month. A revive needs a concrete next step and, for job/side/tool, a receiver (a name, or `me: <why>`); the slate cap and the 7-day clock apply.
- **Sessions**: delete the SAFE list? Recommend yes.
- **Feedback look-back**, first review of the month only (day of month 7 or less): approve reading the meetings? Recommend yes. `FEEDBACK.md` (beside this file) holds the method and privacy rules.

## Step 4 — Apply the answers

- **Sweep**: `python3 $PT/portfolio.py sweep-decide <name> revive|keep|archive [--next-action "<step>"] [--receiver "<who>"]`. A revive refused for the cap or a missing receiver goes back to Eric; the receiver is always his words. Rows he leaves undecided return next week on their own. Commit the registry in project-triage as `data: sweep <YYYY-MM-DD>` and push.
- **Sessions**: `claude rm <id>` for each SAFE id. It refuses a session whose worktree has unpushed work: report the refusal and leave the session. Sessions leave only by `claude rm` of a SAFE id; KEEP sessions and `~/.claude/jobs/` folders stay. Repos with unsaved work go to `/closeout`.
- **Inbox**: move up to 10 entries whose home is a repo or `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`. Drive-bound entries are counted, not moved: the Drive mount hangs on reads, so they go by the Drive MCP or `gws` in their own session.
- **Feedback look-back**, if approved: run `FEEDBACK.md`.

## Step 5 — Synthesize

Read each Step 2 input and build:

- **Theme map**: topics in 2+ sources.
- **Project map**: each named project progressed (decision made, work shipped), drifted (mentioned, no movement), or stuck (blocked, awaiting input).
- **Decision log**: decision sentences across all sources.
- **Stale action items**: Fireflies has no done flag. An item from a meeting 14–30 days old is stale (⚠) unless a source from this week (a `docs/STATUS.md`, the output ledger, a newer meeting) shows it done.
- **Essay clusters**: 2–4 linked Notes on one idea.
- **Movement** on last week's three priorities: a commit that changes the work itself (STATUS-only and closeout-sweep commits do not count), a new line in the output ledger, or a new date written down.

**Curation rule:** a theme, project or decision you cannot state in one sentence with a source citation is dropped. The review is Eric's working memory, not a complete record.

## Step 6 — Write the note

Write `Inbox/weekly-review/YYYY-MM-DD-review.md` (today's date) once, from `Templates/weekly-review.md`, with every Step 2–5 result in it. A section with nothing in it reads "None this week." Every claim carries a source: `[[file]]` or `(meeting: X, date)`.

0. **Last week's three priorities — did they happen?** One line per priority from the previous review: yes / partly / no, with the evidence. A priority with no movement gets a banner as the first line under the note's title: `> ⚠ NO MOVEMENT — week N: <priority>`. N counts the consecutive reviews it appeared in without movement (read back through earlier reviews). At week 3, its line in **Next week — priorities** must be ship by a named date, re-date in writing, or park; carrying it as-is is the drift.
1. **Themes recurring this week**, each with its source.
2. **Active projects — status snapshot**: table of Project | Status (progressing / drifting / stuck / decided / new) | Last touched | Note. Mark "drifting" ruthlessly: that is the value of the exercise.
3. **Decisions made this week**, in Eric's words where available. When the look-back ran, the **Feedback look-back (monthly)** section follows this one (format in `FEEDBACK.md`).
4. **Open action items (stale > 14d flagged)**: owner — task — age — source meeting, ⚠ on stale.
5. **Essay angles emerging**: working title, one-sentence thesis, 2–4 `[[Note]]` links. Candidates for `Drafts/`.
6. **Next week — priorities and why**: three items, ranked, one sentence each on why it beats the alternatives. **The most important section.** Push back if Eric's answer is generic ("keep working on X").
7. **Open threads to revisit**: noticed, not actioned.
8. **Pipeline hygiene**: one line for each item that is not clean; omit the section when all are clean.
   - Meeting filenames: N regressions, N semantic diffs — see meeting-sync drift audit.
   - Registry drift: counts by kind — run `portfolio.py crosswalk`.
   - Unnamed speakers: the UNNAMED meeting titles — "Open in Fireflies and name the Speaker N entries" (Fireflies has no API for it).
   - Generic-titled meetings still in the local DB: suggest `/name-meetings`.
   - Sweep: N revived, N kept, N archived, N still pending (registry commit sha).
   - Sessions: N deleted, N kept.
   - Inbox: N moved; N left in `_INBOX`, N in `~/Downloads`, N of them Drive-bound; up or down from last week.

Set the frontmatter counts: `meetings_reviewed`, `interviews_reviewed`, `notes_touched`.

**Done when** the note exists with every section filled or "None this week.", every non-clean Step 2 result has its Pipeline hygiene line, the frontmatter counts are set, Eric's sweep answers are applied and pushed, and **Next week** holds three ranked priorities, each with its why.

## Step 7 — Sign off

Three to five lines:

- File written: path.
- N meetings, M interviews, K notes synthesized.
- The three priorities for next week.
- The one open decision, with your recommended answer.
- The look-back's top 3, when it ran.

Then offer, and wait: start a `Drafts/<essay-slug>.md` from one essay angle, or carry stale action items into tomorrow's agenda. A draft is written only when Eric picks one.

A revive refused for the cap or a missing receiver goes back to Eric; the receiver is always his words. Rows he leaves undecided return next week on their own. Commit the registry in project-triage as `data: sweep <YYYY-MM-DD>` and push.
- **Sessions**: `claude rm <id>` for each SAFE id. It refuses a session whose worktree has unpushed work: report the refusal and leave the session. Sessions leave only by `claude rm` of a SAFE id; KEEP sessions and `~/.claude/jobs/` folders stay. Repos with unsaved work go to `/closeout`.
- **Inbox**: move up to 10 entries whose home is a repo or `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/`. Drive-bound entries are counted, not moved: the Drive mount hangs on reads, so they go by the Drive MCP or `gws` in their own session.

## Step 5 — Synthesize

Read each Step 2 input and build:

- **Theme map**: topics in 2+ sources.
- **Project map**: each named project progressed (decision made, work shipped), drifted (mentioned, no movement), or stuck (blocked, awaiting input).
- **Decision log**: decision sentences across all sources.
- **Stale action items**: Fireflies has no done flag. An item from a meeting 14–30 days old is stale (⚠) unless a source from this week (a `docs/STATUS.md`, the output ledger, a newer meeting) shows it done.
- **Essay clusters**: 2–4 linked Notes on one idea.
- **Movement** on last week's three priorities: a commit that changes the work itself (STATUS-only and closeout-sweep commits do not count), a new line in the output ledger, or a new date written down.

## Step 6 — Write the note

Write `Inbox/weekly-review/YYYY-MM-DD-review.md` (today's date) once, from `Templates/weekly-review.md`, with every Step 2–5 result in it. A section with nothing in it reads "None this week." Every claim carries a source: `[[file]]` or `(meeting: X, date)`.

A priority with no movement gets a banner as the first line under the note's title: `> ⚠ NO MOVEMENT — week N: <priority>`. N counts the consecutive reviews it appeared in without movement (read back through earlier reviews). At week 3, its line in **Next week — priorities** must be ship by a named date, re-date in writing, or park; carrying it as-is is the drift.
1. **Themes recurring this week**, each with its source.
2. **Active projects — status snapshot**: table of Project | Status (progressing / drifting / stuck / decided / new) | Last touched | Note. Mark "drifting" ruthlessly: that is the value of the exercise.
3. **Decisions made this week**, in Eric's words where available. When the look-back ran, the **Feedback look-back (monthly)** section follows this one (format in `FEEDBACK.md`).
4. **Open action items (stale > 14d flagged)**: owner — task — age — source meeting, ⚠ on stale.
5. **Essay angles emerging**: working title, one-sentence thesis, 2–4 `[[Note]]` links. Candidates for `Drafts/`.
6. **Next week — priorities and why**: three items, ranked, one sentence each on why it beats the alternatives. **The most important section.** Push back if Eric's answer is generic ("keep working on X").
7. **Open threads to revisit**: noticed, not actioned.
8. **Pipeline hygiene**: one line for each item that is not clean; omit the section when all are clean.
   - Meeting filenames: N regressions, N semantic diffs — see meeting-sync drift audit.
   - Registry drift: counts by kind — run `portfolio.py crosswalk`.
   - Unnamed speakers: the UNNAMED meeting titles — "Open in Fireflies and name the Speaker N entries" (Fireflies has no API for it).
   - Generic-titled meetings still in the local DB: suggest `/name-meetings`.
   - Sweep: N revived, N kept, N archived, N still pending (registry commit sha).
   - Sessions: N deleted, N kept.
   - Inbox: N moved; N left in `_INBOX`, N in `~/Downloads`, N of them Drive-bound; up or down from last week.

Set the frontmatter counts: `meetings_reviewed`, `interviews_reviewed`, `notes_touched`.

**Done when** the note exists with every section filled or "None this week.", every non-clean Step 2 result has its Pipeline hygiene line, the frontmatter counts are set, Eric's sweep answers are applied and pushed, and **Next week** holds three ranked priorities, each with its why.

Three to five lines:

- File written: path.
- N meetings, M interviews, K notes synthesized.
- The three priorities for next week.
- The one open decision, with your recommended answer.
- The look-back's top 3, when it ran.

3	description: Run the KeystoneOS daily backup on demand (git-push the memory repos, rsync state to Google Drive and the CRASHBOX SSD, reindex memsearch), then report what was saved and what was skipped. Use when the user says "/backup", "run the backup", "back up now", "back my stuff up", "did the backup run", "the backup failed", "I left the laptop off — catch up the backup", or when a session-start HOOK FAILURE names daily-backup. The scheduled launchd job only fires if the Mac is awake at 21:00, so this is the manual catch-up path. NOT FOR whole-stack health checks (use claude-stack-doctor).
4	---
5	
6	# Backup
7	
8	Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` right now. Same script the `com.keystone.dailybackup`
9	launchd agent runs at 21:00 daily (moved from 09:00 on 2026-09-24, when the Mac became the evening machine) — this is the on-demand path for when the Mac was shut at 21:00.
10	
11	## Run it
12	
13	Do not pre-check anything. Run first, report after.
14	
15	```bash
16	/usr/bin/caffeinate -i /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
17	```
18	
19	Use a Bash `timeout` of `600000` (10 min). An awake run takes ~5-10 min, most of it the memsearch
20	INDEX step. Keep `caffeinate -i`: without it the Mac idle-sleeps on battery the moment the copies
21	finish, and INDEX crawls through brief dark wakes. On 2026-10-06 that turned a ~6 min index into
22	2 h. If a run outlasts the timeout, it moves to the background; wait for it, do not re-run.
23	
24	## Read the verdict from state, not from the tail
25	
26	```bash
27	cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json
28	```
29	
30	`status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. That file is the authority.
31	The tail is for diagnosing, not for deciding.
32	
33	**`status: OK` is not "everything was saved" — read `okCount` too.** A run that skipped the
34	SSD still ends `OK` with 0 errors. See the SSD gotcha below for what the count means.
35	
36	## Then clear the stale hook error, if any
37	
38	A failed run appends a line to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`, which is surfaced
39	as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. A later successful run does **not** clear it. If `status`
40	is now `OK` and the file contains only `daily-backup:` lines, archive and empty it:
41	
42	```bash
43	cat ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log >> ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors-ledger.log
44	cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
45	```
46	
47	If any non-`daily-backup` line is present, leave the file alone and tell the user what else is in it.
48	Shell truncation (`: > file`) under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule
49	`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`, and there is no `truncate` binary here — use `cp /dev/null`.
50	
51	## Report
52	
53	Three lines, plain: did it work, what was skipped, what to do next. Never report "backup complete"
54	without naming a skipped target — a silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to prevent.
55	
56	## Gotchas
57	
58	**Safe to ignore — expected on a healthy run:**
59	- `uv-prune: skipped (locked)` — a live `uvx` process (the browser-use MCP servers) holds the uv cache lock; not an error, retried next run.
60	- `CODEX skip (missing): ~/.codex/<item>` / `SHELL skip (missing): ~/<file>` — that allowlist item does not exist on this machine.
61	- `TARGET baylor deprecated in manifest - snapshots to it SKIPPED` — deliberate.
62	
63	**Real gaps — always surface these to the user:**
64	- `TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED - orphan and working-tree capture SKIPPED`
65	  — the run still reports `OK` with 0 errors, but **untracked, gitignored, and uncommitted-modified
66	  files were not saved anywhere.** GitHub and Google Drive cover only committed and pushed work.
67	  Tell the user to plug in CRASHBOX and run again. This is the most likely way to lose real work.
68	
69	  **Cross-check with `okCount`, because the error count cannot see this.** `okCount` in
70	  `backup-state.json` is the number of jobs that ran, and two whole job classes — `CAPTURE`
71	  (per-project working-tree files) and `STATE-SSD` — exist only when the SSD is mounted. So:
72	  - **~31 jobs** = SSD captured. **~9-10 jobs** = SSD was absent; only the 4 `REPO` pushes and
73	    6 Drive `SNAP`s ran (verified against runs on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05).
74	  - A single-digit `okCount` with `status: OK` is the silent partial backup. Say so out loud.
75	  - Do not derive this from the error count or the exit code — both read `OK` either way.
76	- `TARGET ... NOT MOUNTED - is Google Drive for Desktop running?` — the Drive app is not running.
77	  Start it, then re-run.
78	- `PUSH ERR ... Could not resolve host: github.com` — a network blip, not a repo problem. Confirm
79	  with `ping -c1 github.com`, then just re-run; the commits are already made locally and will push.
80	  (Seen 2026-09-04 09:05: both `global-memory` and `skills` failed this way and a re-run fixed both.)
81	- `repo-diverged:<name>` — automation will never merge. Reconcile that repo by hand. For
82	  `dotclaude` and `global-memory` this almost always means the other machine pushed; `/dev-sync`
83	  Step 1 merges and pushes both (seen 2026-09-15).
84	- `STATE-SSD .codex : FAILED` with `rsync: error: skills/<name>: unlinkat: Directory not empty`
85	  just above it in `daily-backup.log` (the error only reaches the log file, not stdout). Cause:
86	  `sync-to-codex.sh` turned `~/.codex/skills/<name>` into a symlink, but the SSD copy is still a
87	  real folder. The copy is additive (no `--delete`, no `--force`), so rsync cannot swap a
88	  non-empty folder for a link — and it reports only some names per run, so fixing one reveals the
89	  next. List them all at once:
90	  `cd ~/.codex/skills && for e in *; do [ -L "$e" ] && [ -d "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && [ ! -L "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && echo "$e"; done`
91	  Move each one (literal paths — dcg blocks `mv` with `$VAR` paths) into
92	  `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/_OLD_codex-skills-dirs-<date>/`, then re-run. Never `rm`:
93	  the skills also live in the `claude-skills` repo, but the move is free. (Seen 2026-09-15:
94	  `dev-sync`, `new-project`, `startup`, `closeout`.)
95	
96	**Other:**
97	- A nightly INDEX that takes hours (`INDEX path set` to `INDEX full set` in `daily-backup.log`) is the
98	  Mac asleep, not memsearch. With the lid closed at 21:00, launchd's `caffeinate -i -s` cannot keep it
99	  awake, so INDEX runs only in short dark wakes (`pmset -g log | grep Sleep` shows it). It still finishes.
100	- Every log line appears **twice** for launchd runs and once for manual runs. The script both writes
101	  to the log file and prints to stdout, and the plist captures stdout to the same file. Not a bug —
102	  do not "fix" it, and do not read doubled lines as two attempts.
103	- The script is PowerShell only because `pwsh` runs it natively. It manages launchd, not Task
104	  Scheduler; the Windows original (`daily-backup.ps1.win-orig`) was removed 2026-10-23 and is in dotclaude git history.
105	- `-DryRun` is the only parameter. Use it to preview without writing.
106	
107	## Examples
108	
109	**Example 1: routine catch-up**
110	```
111	User: "run the backup"
112	→ Runs the script, reads backup-state.json (status OK, 0 errors)
113	→ "Backup done, no errors. Everything pushed and copied to Drive.
114	   CRASHBOX SSD wasn't plugged in, so uncommitted files were not saved.
115	   Plug it in and run /backup again if you have unsaved work."
116	```
117	
118	**Example 2: session start shows a hook failure**
119	```
120	User: "the backup failed this morning — fix it"
121	→ Greps daily-backup.log for the error codes → DNS failure on both pushes
122	→ Confirms github.com reachable, re-runs the script → status OK
123	→ Archives and empties .errors.log so the warning stops appearing
124	```

  `cd ~/.codex/skills && for e in *; do [ -L "$e" ] && [ -d "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && [ ! -L "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && echo "$e"; done`

`com.keystone.clouddrivepush` (07:00 and 17:30) failed under launchd from 2026-10-12 to 10-23 with rsync `open: Operation not permitted` on `Drive/.../_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/`. By hand from Terminal it always worked.

**Cause (tested 2026-10-23).** A process started straight by launchd (python3 or bash) can stat, mkdir and create new files in the Drive mount, and rewrite files it made itself. It cannot list Drive folders, or open, rename over, or delete files that Terminal made. Each such file carries `com.apple.macl` naming Terminal; `xattr -d` does not remove it. Full Disk Access on `Python.app`/rsync does not help (tried 10-14). rsync lists the destination, so it failed on the first step.

**Fix (live 2026-10-23).** The plist runs `/bin/bash ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`. That runs `open -g -a Terminal ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command`, which runs `cloud-push.py` (rsync, unchanged) with Terminal's access. The launcher waits 90 s for a new `START` line in `cloud-push.log`; if none, it writes an ERROR to the log and to `.errors.log`. Tracked plist copy: `~/.claude/scripts/com.keystone.clouddrivepush.plist`. Proven: kickstarted runs OK 07:15 and 07:21 with the screen locked.

**Known costs.** Each run opens a Terminal window. Eric set profile "Clear Dark" to "Close if the shell exited cleanly" (10-23, in Terminal Settings; a `defaults import` did not reach the running Terminal), so the window closes when the copy ends (tested). Under memory pressure Terminal ran queued opens ~5 min late; the 90 s check would log that as an ERROR even if the copy runs later.

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Any other launchd job that must read or change Terminal-made Drive files hits the same wall; route it through Terminal the same way or use the `gws` API. See [[automation-cadence]] and [[cloud-copy-approval]].

#!/bin/bash
# Gate for daily-backup.ps1. Both launchd jobs call it:
#   com.keystone.dailybackup        hourly 12:00-17:00, so a failed try gets another chance
#   com.keystone.dailybackup-login  at login, so a Mac that was off still gets a backup
# Runs the backup only when: no run ended OK today, the Mac is on AC power, no backup is
# running, and fewer than 2 real runs started today (a lasting error must not run 6 times).
# Why daytime + AC: every 21:00 run from 10-13 to 10-22 ended ERROR because the Mac slept
# on battery, and caffeinate -s only holds sleep off on AC (audit 2026-10-22).
# shortcut: checks the log, not a lock file; two runs at the same moment could both start.
LOG="${BACKUP_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log}"
TODAY=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
skip() { echo "$(date '+%F %T') gate skip: $1"; exit 0; }

grep -q "^$TODAY .*daily-backup end: OK" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null && skip "already OK today"
pmset -g ps | grep -q "AC Power" || skip "on battery"
# [.] keeps the pattern from matching any shell whose command line merely mentions the script
pgrep -f "pwsh.*daily-backup[.]ps1" >/dev/null && skip "a backup is already running"
STARTS=$(grep -c "^$TODAY .*daily-backup start (DryRun=False)" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)
[ "${STARTS:-0}" -ge 2 ] && skip "2 tries already today"

exec /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1"

#!/bin/bash
# Gate for daily-backup.ps1. Both launchd jobs call it:
#   com.keystone.dailybackup        hourly 12:00-17:00, so a failed try gets another chance
#   com.keystone.dailybackup-login  at login, so a Mac that was off still gets a backup
# Runs the backup only when: no run ended OK today, the Mac is on AC power, no backup is
# running, and fewer than 2 real runs started today (a lasting error must not run 6 times).
# Why daytime + AC: every 21:00 run from 10-13 to 10-22 ended ERROR because the Mac slept
# on battery, and caffeinate -s only holds sleep off on AC (audit 2026-10-22).
# shortcut: checks the log, not a lock file; two runs at the same moment could both start.
LOG="${BACKUP_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log}"
TODAY=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
skip() { echo "$(date '+%F %T') gate skip: $1"; exit 0; }

grep -q "^$TODAY .*daily-backup end: OK" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null && skip "already OK today"
pmset -g ps | grep -q "AC Power" || skip "on battery"
# [.] keeps the pattern from matching any shell whose command line merely mentions the script
pgrep -f "pwsh.*daily-backup[.]ps1" >/dev/null && skip "a backup is already running"
STARTS=$(grep -c "^$TODAY .*daily-backup start (DryRun=False)" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)
[ "${STARTS:-0}" -ge 2 ] && skip "2 tries already today"

exec /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1"

---
name: backup
description: Run the KeystoneOS daily backup now (git-push the memory repos, rsync to Google Drive and the CRASHBOX SSD, reindex memsearch) and report what was saved and what was skipped. Use when the user says "/backup", "run the backup", "back up now", "did the backup run", "the backup failed", "catch up the backup", or when a session-start HOOK FAILURE names daily-backup. Do not use for whole-stack health checks (use claude-stack-doctor).
---

# Backup

Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` now: the manual catch-up for the scheduled job. Schedule and run conditions (login + hourly, AC power, 2 real tries a day) live in the header of `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`, the gate both launchd jobs call. A manual run skips the gate, counts toward its 2 tries, and an OK stops the hourly job for the rest of the day.

## Steps

1. **Check for a live run.** `pgrep -f "pwsh.*daily-backup[.]ps1"`. If one is running, wait for it and go to step 3 for its result instead of starting a second.
2. **Run it** with Bash `run_in_background: true` and wait for the completion notice. A run takes ~10 min awake; a sleeping Mac stretches it to hours.
   ```bash
   /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```
3. **Read the verdict from state.** `cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json`. It counts only when `dryRun` is `false` and `lastRun` is this run (a `-DryRun` overwrites the file too). `status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. The state is the authority; the tail is for diagnosis.
4. **Read this run's log section** for what the state cannot show. Take the run id from the newest `daily-backup start (DryRun=False) run=<id>` line, then:
   ```bash
   awk '/daily-backup start .*run=<id>/,/daily-backup end/' ~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log | grep -E 'NOT MOUNTED|MANIFEST|SECRET-SCAN|ERR|FAILED'
   ```
   `TARGET SSD ... NOT MOUNTED` means the run ends `OK` with 0 errors, yet untracked, gitignored and uncommitted files were saved nowhere: GitHub and Drive hold only committed, pushed work. This silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to catch.
5. **Fix each error code** with `FIXES.md` (beside this file), then re-run from step 1. Stop after one re-run and report what is left.
6. **Clear `.errors.log`.** A later OK run does not clear it, and it shows as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. When `status` is `OK` and every line in `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` starts with `daily-backup:`, archive and empty it:
   ```bash
   cat ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log >> ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors-ledger.log
   cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
   ```
   Report a `secret-scan warning` line before archiving it: give the file names it lists and say "warn-only, check and rotate if real". Read only the names; the session `.jsonl` files themselves stay closed, since they may hold the secret. Any line from another job: leave the file as it is and tell Eric what it holds. (`cp /dev/null` because dcg blocks `: > file` under `$HOME` and there is no `truncate`.)
7. **Report**, three plain lines: did it work, what was skipped (name the SSD when it was absent), what to do next.

**Done when** the state shows this real run, every error code is fixed or reported with its cause, any skipped target is named, and `.errors.log` is cleared or its other lines are reported.

## Normal on a healthy run

- `uv-prune: skipped (locked ...)`: a live `uvx` server holds the uv cache lock; retried next run.
- `CODEX skip (missing)` / `SHELL skip (missing)`: that allowlist item does not exist on this machine.
- `TARGET baylor deprecated in manifest - snapshots to it SKIPPED`: deliberate.
- `MANIFEST N declared dir(s) absent from disk`: a log line, not an error.
- Every log line appears twice for launchd runs, once for manual runs: the script prints to stdout and the plist sends stdout to the same file. Doubled lines are one attempt.

# Backup fixes, by error code or log line

Reached from step 5 of `SKILL.md`. Codes come from `errors` in `backup-state.json`; log lines from the run's section of `daily-backup.log`.

## `TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED`

Not an error code (`optional: true` in the manifest). Tell Eric to plug in CRASHBOX and run `/backup` again. This is the most likely way to lose real work.

## `manifest-unmanaged:<dir>`

A folder in `~/DEV` has no entry in `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json` (default-deny: an undeclared folder is an error, not a skip). Add a `paths` entry shaped like its neighbours: `path` (`DEV/<dir>`), `class`, `isRepo`, `remote`, `destinations`, `captureOrphans`, `captureWorkingTree`, and a `note` saying why. A folder that may hold athlete or health data goes `destinations: ["ssd"]` only, like `_ARCHIVE` and `_to_delete`. Commit the manifest in the `~/.claude` (dotclaude) repo.

## `backup-target-offline:GoogleDrive/_MACHINE` or `TARGET ... NOT MOUNTED - is Google Drive for Desktop running?`

The Drive app is not running. Start it, then re-run.

## `repo-push:<name>` with `Could not resolve host: github.com`

A network blip. Confirm with `ping -c1 github.com`, then re-run; the commits are made locally and will push.

## `repo-diverged:<name>`

Automation never merges. For `dotclaude` and `global-memory` it almost always means another machine pushed: `/dev-sync` Step 1 merges and pushes both.

## `index-incomplete:<run>` or a slow INDEX step

The Mac slept. A run whose `INDEX path set` to `INDEX full set` takes hours ran INDEX only in short dark wakes (`pmset -g log | grep Sleep` shows them); `caffeinate -s` holds sleep off only on AC power. It still finishes. The 10-28 13:00 run took 2 h 52 min this way.

## `snapshot-ssd` with `STATE-SSD .codex : FAILED` and `rsync: error: skills/<name>: unlinkat: Directory not empty`

The error reaches only `daily-backup.log`, not stdout. `sync-to-codex.sh` made `~/.codex/skills/<name>` a symlink while the SSD copy is still a real folder; the copy is additive (no `--delete`, no `--force`), so rsync cannot swap them, and it names only some per run. List them all:

```bash
cd ~/.codex/skills && for e in *; do [ -L "$e" ] && [ -d "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && [ ! -L "/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/codex/skills/$e" ] && echo "$e"; done
```

Move each one (literal paths: dcg blocks `mv` with `$VAR` paths) into `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/_OLD_codex-skills-dirs-<date>/`, then re-run. Move, never `rm`.

## Any other code

Find the code's `$Errors.Add(` line in `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` and read the block around it. `-DryRun` is the script's only parameter: use it to test a fix without writing.

# Backup fixes, by error code or log line

Reached from step 5 of `SKILL.md`. Codes come from `errors` in `backup-state.json`; log lines from the run's section of `daily-backup.log`.

## `TARGET SSD /Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup NOT MOUNTED`

Not an error code (`optional: true` in the manifest). Tell Eric to plug in CRASHBOX and run `/backup` again. This is the most likely way to lose real work.

## `manifest-unmanaged:<dir>`

A folder in `~/DEV` has no entry in `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json` (default-deny: an undeclared folder is an error, not a skip). Add a `paths` entry shaped like its neighbours: `path` (`DEV/<dir>`), `class`, `isRepo`, `remote`, `destinations`, `captureOrphans`, `captureWorkingTree`, and a `note` saying why. A folder that may hold athlete or health data goes `destinations: ["ssd"]` only, like `_ARCHIVE` and `_to_delete`. Commit the manifest in the `~/.claude` (dotclaude) repo.

## `backup-target-offline:GoogleDrive/_MACHINE` or `TARGET ... NOT MOUNTED - is Google Drive for Desktop running?`

The Drive app is not running. Start it, then re-run.

## `repo-push:<name>` with `Could not resolve host: github.com`

A network blip. Confirm with `ping -c1 github.com`, then re-run; the commits are made locally and will push.

## `repo-diverged:<name>`

Automation never merges. For `dotclaude` and `global-memory` it almost always means another machine pushed: `/dev-sync` Step 1 merges and pushes both.

## `index-incomplete:<run>` or a slow INDEX step

The Mac slept. A run whose `INDEX path set` to `INDEX full set` takes hours ran INDEX only in short dark wakes (`pmset -g log | grep Sleep` shows them); `caffeinate -s` holds sleep off only on AC power. It still finishes. The 10-28 13:00 run took 2 h 52 min this way.

## `snapshot-ssd` with `STATE-SSD .codex : FAILED` and `rsync: error: skills/<name>: unlinkat: Directory not empty`

The error reaches only `daily-backup.log`, not stdout. `sync-to-codex.sh` made `~/.codex/skills/<name>` a symlink while the SSD copy is still a real folder; the copy is additive (no `--delete`, no `--force`), so rsync cannot swap them, and it names only some per run. List them all:


Move each one (literal paths: dcg blocks `mv` with `$VAR` paths) into `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/_OLD_codex-skills-dirs-<date>/`, then re-run. Move, never `rm`.

# Backup

Runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` now: the manual catch-up for the scheduled job. Schedule and run conditions (login + hourly, AC power, 2 real tries a day) live in the header of `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup-login.sh`, the gate both launchd jobs call. A manual run skips the gate, counts toward its 2 tries, and an OK stops the hourly job for the rest of the day.

## Steps

1. **Check for a live run.** `pgrep -f "pwsh.*daily-backup[.]ps1"`. If one is running, wait for it and go to step 3 for its result instead of starting a second.
2. **Run it** with Bash `run_in_background: true` and wait for the completion notice. A run takes ~10 min awake; a sleeping Mac stretches it to hours.
   ```bash
   /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```
3. **Read the verdict from state.** `cat ~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json`. It counts only when `dryRun` is `false` and `lastRun` is this run (a `-DryRun` overwrites the file too). `status` is `OK` or `ERROR`; `errors` lists the failed job codes. The state is the authority; the tail is for diagnosis.
4. **Read this run's log section** for what the state cannot show. Take the run id from the newest `daily-backup start (DryRun=False) run=<id>` line, then:
   ```bash
   awk '/daily-backup start .*run=<id>/,/daily-backup end/' ~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log | grep -E 'NOT MOUNTED|MANIFEST|SECRET-SCAN|ERR|FAILED'
   ```
   `TARGET SSD ... NOT MOUNTED` means the run ends `OK` with 0 errors, yet untracked, gitignored and uncommitted files were saved nowhere: GitHub and Drive hold only committed, pushed work. This silent partial backup is the failure this skill exists to catch.
5. **Fix each error code** with `FIXES.md` (beside this file), then re-run from step 1. Stop after one re-run and report what is left.
6. **Clear `.errors.log`.** A later OK run does not clear it, and it shows as a HOOK FAILURE at every session start. When `status` is `OK` and every line in `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` starts with `daily-backup:`, archive and empty it:
   ```bash
   cat ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log >> ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors-ledger.log
   cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
   ```
   Report a `secret-scan warning` line before archiving it: give the file names it lists and say "warn-only, check and rotate if real". Read only the names; the session `.jsonl` files themselves stay closed, since they may hold the secret. Any line from another job: leave the file as it is and tell Eric what it holds. (`cp /dev/null` because dcg blocks `: > file` under `$HOME` and there is no `truncate`.)
7. **Report**, three plain lines: did it work, what was skipped (name the SSD when it was absent), what to do next.

**Done when** the state shows this real run, every error code is fixed or reported with its cause, any skipped target is named, and `.errors.log` is cleared or its other lines are reported.

## Normal on a healthy run

- `uv-prune: skipped (locked ...)`: a live `uvx` server holds the uv cache lock; retried next run.
- `CODEX skip (missing)` / `SHELL skip (missing)`: that allowlist item does not exist on this machine.
- `TARGET baylor deprecated in manifest - snapshots to it SKIPPED`: deliberate.
- `MANIFEST N declared dir(s) absent from disk`: a log line, not an error.
- Every log line appears twice for launchd runs, once for manual runs: the script prints to stdout and the plist sends stdout to the same file. Doubled lines are one attempt.

content.text:
I audited the **backup** skill and fixed it. I chose it because there is no written audit list anywhere. It is the last daily maintenance skill not yet reviewed. Then I tested the new skill by running a real backup with it.

**What was wrong:**
- **Wrong schedule.** The skill said 21:00. The real job runs when you log in and every hour from 12:00 to 17:00, at most 2 tries a day.
- **A test run could hide a failure.** A dry run (a practice run that saves nothing) overwrites the "last result" file. Today both real runs failed, but that file said "OK."
- **A bug in the scheduler.** A dry run also writes "OK" to the log, and the scheduler read that as "today's backup is done." It could skip a real backup. I fixed it and added a test (5 of 5 pass).
- **Stale or missing advice.** One error message the skill explained no longer exists. Today's real error (`manifest-unmanaged`) was not covered. Secret-scan warnings were cleared without being reported to you.
- **Layout.** The skill now has steps and a "Done when" line. The fixes for each error moved to `~/.claude/skills/backup/FIXES.md`.

**The test run worked:**
- The backup ran from 15:58 to 16:14 with status OK and 0 errors. Today now has a good backup.
- The CRASHBOX SSD was not plugged in. Uncommitted and untracked files were not saved anywhere.
- One secret-scan warning on `b1b9233e...jsonl`. At 12:00 today, closeout checked the same file and called it a false alarm. I did not open the file. This warning only flags it; it does not block anything.
- The run showed me two more skill fixes, which I made.

**What you do now:** nothing is required. If you want the uncommitted files saved too, plug in CRASHBOX and type `/backup`.

**Not checked:** I ran the backup once, by hand. I did not test the login and hourly launchd runs with the new scheduler fix; tomorrow's first hourly run will be its first real use. The backup's own auto-commit also swept 3 deleted `.trash` files in the skills repo into `e5f9261`. Those deletions were not mine.

1	---
2	name: meeting-sync
3	description: >-
4	  Sync new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault; audit vault filenames for
5	  drift against Fireflies titles. Idempotent. Use when the user says "sync meetings",
6	  "pull latest meetings", "/meeting-sync", "update meeting notes", "any new meetings?",
7	  or when invoked by weekly-review. Also for filename drift — "are any meeting files
8	  misnamed?", "did a meeting get renamed after export?", "why is this meeting titled
9	  differently in Fireflies than in the vault?", "audit the meeting filenames". Do not
10	  use to rename generic titles inside Fireflies (use name-meetings) or to search what
11	  was said in transcripts (use pp-fireflies).
12	argument-hint: "[days-back]"
13	---
14	
15	# Meeting Sync
16	
17	Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.
18	
19	## Paths — shared config
20	
21	Vault and state-file paths live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (single source of truth):
22	- `vault_inbox_meetings` — platform-specific export target
23	- `meeting_sync_state_file` — idempotency ledger (`.sync-state.json` in that folder)
24	- `meeting_lookback_days` — default window (14)
25	
26	`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.
27	
28	sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.
29	
30	## Prerequisite — one-time auth
31	
32	Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:
33	
34	> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. On the Mac, store the key in the Keychain with `security add-generic-password -U -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w` (it prompts for the key; `~/.zshrc` exports it); on Windows, set it under System Properties → Environment Variables. Then open a new terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.
35	
36	Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.
37	
38	## Sync flow
39	
40	### 1. Run the pipeline script
41	
42	The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:
43	
44	**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
45	```bash
46	python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
47	```
48	Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.
49	
50	**Phase B — export:**
51	```bash
52	python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
53	```
54	Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.
55	
56	`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.
57	
58	### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)
59	
60	The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).
61	
62	- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
63	- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
64	- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.
65	
66	This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.
67	
68	### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)
69	
70	For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.
71	
72	Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.
73	
74	### 4. Tag each exported file with its project (script's job)
75	
76	After the header is in place, pass the same paths to the tagger:
77	
78	```bash
79	python scripts/tag_project.py <path> [<path> ...]
80	```
81	
82	It asks TypeSafe's Jev which `portfolio.json` project each meeting is mainly about, and adds `- project/<PortfolioName>` under `## Project tags` only when the answer is confident. It always adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line recording what was asked and answered, which is also how a rerun knows to skip the note. `meeting-prep` reads the `- project/` line to find a project's meetings.
83	
84	It never blocks the sync: no key, no network or no transcript just leaves the note untagged and logs to stderr. Relay any `WARNING` lines. Run it only after step 3, because notes without a `## Project tags` header are skipped.
85	
86	## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)
87	
88	A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.
89	
90	```bash
91	python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
92	```
93	
94	Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.
95	
96	It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:
97	
98	- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
99	- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
100	- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.
101	
102	Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.
103	
104	## Output to user
105	
106	When done, report:
107	- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
108	- M new exports written, K tagged with a project
109	- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
110	- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."
111	
112	Keep it to 3 lines.
113	
114	## Error handling
115	
116	sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.
117	
118	- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
119	- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
120	- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
121	- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.
122	
123	## Gotchas
124	
125	- **Two tag vocabularies share `## Project tags`.** Hand tags are topic words (`project/rtp`, `project/load-monitoring`). Jev tags are exact `portfolio.json` names (`project/Sport_Tech_Vetting`). The tagger only appends and never edits or removes a hand tag.
126	- **Measured before shipping, so don't tune the question here.** The question wording and the 0.60 threshold in `tag_project.py` were tested blind on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, 2026-09-22). Jev was confident on 36, and right on 33 of those. It never confidently tagged a non-project meeting, but it found only 7 of 11 real project meetings. OKRs_2026-27 was the repeat miss. Judge any wording change against meetings the test didn't use.
127	- **A missing tag is not evidence the meeting is unrelated.** The marker line says `none of these` or `(unsure)`. Callers still fall back to text search.
128	- **Probabilities wobble by a few points between runs** (for example 0.83 vs 0.81 on the same note). Notes near 0.60 can go either way, which is one reason the marker is written once and not re-asked.
129	- **Vault notes can mix CRLF and LF lines.** The tagger splices in its lines and never re-encodes the file. Don't "clean up" line endings in this script: an earlier draft did, and rewrote about 50 lines of one note.
130	
131	## What NOT to do
132	
133	- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
134	- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
135	- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
136	- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
137	- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
138	- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.
139

1	---
2	name: fireflies-intake
3	description: >-
4	  One-command Fireflies pipeline — sync new meeting transcripts into the SecondBrain
